A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MapDream, and all supplied pages, equations, tables and figures are readable and matchable. Both end with references; neither contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original R2R-CE and RxR-CE evaluations, ablation results and a Unitree G1 real-world navigation demonstration in Sections 4.3–4.6.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations and robot demonstration, including the numerical results in Tables 1–5.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 retain the same autoregressive three-channel BEV generator, map-conditioned action policy, supervised pretraining, action/format rewards and joint GRPO fine-tuning.

E1.justification: Both use R2R-CE and RxR-CE, IRef-VLA landmark annotations, R2R-only training for transfer to RxR-CE, and monocular indoor deployment on Unitree G1. No dataset or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1 and 2 are identical. Aux-Think remains the same comparator despite citation consolidation; newly cited works are not added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: The validation-unseen splits, monocular settings, NE/OSR/SR/SPL metrics, transfer protocol, training sample counts, model configurations and training budgets are unchanged, as are the ablation configurations.

E4.justification: Tables 3–5 retain the same staged-training, channel-initialization and resolution/token-budget ablations. Figures 3–4 retain the same trajectory/map comparison and real-world case study.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, variability estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and the qualitative evidence match. Table 1 retains MapDream SR/SPL of 59.8/54.4 on R2R-CE and 59.4/49.2 on RxR-CE.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, map-channel definitions, reward construction and the joint policy/map probability ratio are unchanged. Neither version presents additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about task-driven map learning, joint map-policy optimization, state-of-the-art monocular performance and generalization.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning transferable spatial structure, channel insensitivity and compact maps are retained. Both acknowledge the absence of persistent global mapping and explicitly enforced temporal map consistency.

D1.justification: v3 adds an abstract statement announcing code/data availability and a project-page link, which v1 lacks. Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and training times in Section 4.2 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Dust to Tower, ThinkMatter, UAV state estimation, GSLAMOT and MambaVO, plus Langley's writing paper in the bibliography. These are limited citation additions; the positioning against existing mapping and VLN approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main prose and section order are essentially unchanged. Edits include the resource announcement, internship/contact/publication notes, author-year citation conventions, bibliographic updates and consolidation of duplicate Aux-Think references.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a document-wide ICML layout: redesigned title/author/abstract area, affiliations moved to footnotes, running headers, revised paragraph/heading/caption styling, and resized or repositioned tables. This substantially changes presentation while preserving all four scientific figures and five tables.

improvement.justification: The new code/data access information provides a useful route to reproducibility materials that v1 omitted. Scientific methods, evidence and limitations remain unchanged, so the benefit is limited to documentation and accessibility. The PDFs do not establish the linked resources' availability or completeness.
